items.what_the_person_sees: 'There is no README task in Quote Page's task list ... I can search the records for it.' / 'I can't see a licence choice ... I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look through the earlier notes and decisions for it?' / 'I haven't set any budget in this conversation' / 'There was no card about the first page in this project' / 'The pizza oven is probably in the Bakery project ... Should I look?'. LC-C10: 3 of 12 past questions named the right record with its date (pass needs 10), 5 said a recorded thing is missing; in Quote Page 1 of 11 past questions called recall.

items.root_cause_at_head: evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:14 ('You answer fast and short from what you are given'), :38-39 (the lookup tools listed without recall), :68 ('If nothing you were given or looked up holds the answer, say what you looked through': a sanctioned way out with no lookup); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:616-617 CHAT_RECALL_RULES ('The first message holds what is true now ... Answer questions about now from the first message without a lookup') reads to a low-effort model as if task-list questions are 'now'; agent.ts:2029-2095 the claim guard checks only change and ask claims (claims.ts:139 claimOf), nothing compares an absence or 'Should I look?' reply with the turn's recall calls; packages/runtime/src/conversation/project-facts.ts tasksBlock (called at agent.ts:2912) names tasks by current title only, so a renamed task ('Write the README', now 'Write the guide') is invisible without recall; the 12-turn history (transcript.ts:267) then replays the model's own offers, and later misses copy them.
items.fix_sketch: (1) Code guard beside the claim guard (agent.ts ~2029-2095, built like claimOf/claimNudge): absenceOf(text) in claims.ts matches English and German absence or offer-to-look wording ('there is no', 'I can't see/find', 'I found no record', 'nothing ... mentions', 'I haven't searched', 'Should I look/search', 'I can search', 'keine ... gefunden', 'nicht gefunden', 'soll ich nachsehen'); when recall is in the turn's tools and the turn called neither recall nor recall_open, one nudge step inside CHAT_MAX_MODEL_CALLS and the turn's budget, its text not streamed (CHECKING_STEP reset, step line 'Looking through everything recorded…'): 'You said it is not there without looking it up. Call recall now with the person's words and other words for it (an earlier name, another language), then answer from what it returns. Never ask whether to look.' With no call left the reply stays; log the guard on the chat.reply row. Optional (cut line): when the model still makes no lookup, code runs recall with the line's words and hands the hits to one more step. (2) Prompt (conversation-agent.md next version, CHAT_RECALL_RULES; both asserted verbatim on the request): :14 '... from what you are given and what you look up'; :38 list recall and recall_open among the lookup tools; :68 'When what you were given does not hold the answer, look it up with recall in this turn; if recall finds nothing, say what it looked through.'; CHAT_RECALL_RULES adds 'A lookup reads only and needs no yes: never offer to look something up or ask whether to, look it up in this turn. A question about a task, decision, card, document or something said that the first message does not answer needs a lookup. Never say where something probably is (another project) without looking; recall with project all.' (3) Deterministic: a task line in the facts names its earlier title from the change log ('"Write the guide" (earlier "Write the README"): Done, merged'), within the facts' token budget.

items.title: Chat asks a yes/no question in its own words ('Should I look?', 'Shall I set ...?', 'Do you want me to start a session?') and the person's 'yes' gets 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes.'
items.what_the_person_sees: 'I haven't searched the earlier conversation and decisions yet. Should I look for it?' -> 'yes' -> 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes.' (0 model calls, 219 ms). 'This widens what research may read, so I need your yes first. Shall I set research for Reading rules to any public website again?' with no buttons -> 'yes' -> 'Yes to what?'; the rule stays (card on the first try in 1 of 3 fresh projects). 'Do you want me to start a session on Garden club (up to CHF 1)?' with no card -> 'ok'/'yes' -> 'Yes to what?', which also does not say how to start.

items.root_cause_at_head: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1215-1219 answers every bare yes before any model call unless a card waits or liveOffer (agent.ts:893-896) finds the app's own go_ahead offer, so a question the model wrote in prose is invisible and the yes gets YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY (agent.ts:527, via nothingWaitingReply :2592-2605); packages/runtime/src/conversation/claims.ts:69-106 ASKED and :108-119 CHANGED match only past-tense first-person claims, so claimOf (:139) returns null for 'Shall I set ...?' / 'it needs your yes first' and the guard (agent.ts:2045-2074) never nudges the model to call the command; evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:20-21 promises the model that '"yes" ... refer[s] to' its earlier replies; YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY names no next step.
items.fix_sketch: (a) Guard (claims.ts, agent.ts claim-guard region): a third claim kind 'asks': a sentence that asks the person for a yes in words to make a change ('Shall I / Should I / Do you want me to / Want me to / Soll ich' + a change verb: set, change, widen, allow, start, run, add, cancel, pause, raise ...; or '(I|it|this) need(s) your yes|confirmation|approval' next to such a question); clarifying questions without a change verb stay free ('Which project?'); EARLIER and NEGATION filters kept. Counted false when no command of the turn read a change back; claimNudge's lead for it: 'Your reply asks the person for a yes in words, but no command in this turn read a change back, and a typed yes reaches no one. If the person asked for a change, call its command now; the runtime reads it back with Yes and No. Otherwise answer again without asking for a yes.' Still standing after the nudge -> trueLine's NOTHING_CHANGED_REPLY as today. (b) Backstop at agent.ts:1215: when the newest turn is a model answer (no notice, no pendingId, no actions, no go_ahead offer) whose text without its read-back ends in a question, a bare yes or ok goes to the model with the history instead of 'Yes to what?'; that forwarded turn inherits the previous turn's recordsRead, so every change it leads to is read back first; a lookup offer then runs recall, a hand-over offer calls answer_thoroughly (the app's ask line with figures and Go ahead), a start offer calls session_start (the D6 read-back, nothing starts before its Yes). 'Yes to what?' stays for a yes after a statement, a notice, an answered card or nothing. (c) Words: YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY gains a next step: 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes. Say what you want done, for example "run it now" to start a session.' (d) Prompt: 'Never ask for a yes in words ("Shall I ...?"): call the command and the runtime asks with Yes and No; to offer a start, say "say run it now or press Start".'; rewrite :20-21 so it no longer says a bare yes reaches the model. Mirror (b) and (c) in apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts (:4428); design §3.9's '"yes" with no card' line and user-guide.md:400 change (session lead / this area).
items.test_boundary: Composed chat in packages/runtime/test/conversation-memory.test.ts (scripted provider, the l3-chat-claims setup) asserting the nudge request, the read-back card and the second model call that holds the question and the 'yes'; claims unit cases (claimOf non-null for the three live replies and 'Do you want me to start a session on Garden club?', null for 'Which project do you mean?'); real-daemon cases in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts (describe 'l4-chat-answers, run L4') through POST /projects/:id/chat on the stand-in; a UI case in apps/ui/test/chat.test.tsx typing 'yes' under a model question.
items.notes: Three findings, one root (the bare-yes guard plus a claim guard that cannot see a yes asked in words); LC-C17's step key is here (its other two partial reasons are L4-chat-210 decimals and L4-chat-207 the dependency line; the model's prose restating a read-back, 'Starting a session ... needs your yes ... Confirm to start it.', is the selftasks group's L4-selftasks-126). Cross-group duplicate: L4-selftasks-118 (the selftasks group) is the same claims.ts/transcript.ts root (an imitated read-back question and a forged 'The app did:' line): the session lead keeps ONE owner for claims.ts and replyInHistory; this triage proposes that L4-selftasks-118 moves into l4-chat-answers (its asked-claim part joins (a) here, its marker part joins L4-chat-112). Security: a forwarded yes cannot change anything by itself; it inherits recordsRead so a change after a record is read back; no record text becomes an instruction. The hand-over trigger of the same dead end ('Should I go ahead?') is also closed in L4-chat-202 (the model stops writing its own ask); both together are safe in either merge order.

items.root_cause_at_head: packages/commands/src/commands/summary.ts:79 (chatProjectSummary) and :46 (textOf/spokenProjectSummary) read summary_cache.last_session.summary as written, never through resultAfterWait (packages/runtime/src/daemon/run-indicator.ts:60, daemon-only, no port into commands); packages/runtime/src/conversation/project-facts.ts lastSessionBlock (:173-177) gives the chat model the stored text too; apps/ui/src/pages/project/SummaryTab.tsx:141 reloads the summary only when [statusLine, progress] change, and with an open failed-task card the status line ('Waiting for you: ...') does not change on Cancel.
items.fix_sketch: A CommandPorts port resultNow(projectId, since, text) (append-only in packages/commands/src/types.ts), wired in compose to run-indicator's resultAfterWait; chatProjectSummary and textOf/spokenProjectSummary pass last_session.ended_at as since; project-facts' lastSessionBlock applies resultAfterWait before the text goes into the chat facts. SummaryCard's reload key adds this project's run-indicator keys (useRunning(projectId).map(r => r.key)) or reloads on project.changed for this id, which Cancel already emits; the Cancel handlers need no reload of their own. Mirror in apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts (its Cancel already rewrites the words at :3429).

items.title: After Make one project, the closed project's lessons never reach the kept project's sessions
items.what_the_person_sees: Lessons learned in the project that was joined into another ('use the club's dark blue') are read by chat recall but no specialist of the kept project hears them: the next session repeats a mistake the closed project had learned from.
items.evidence: /tmp/frbench/leftovers-C4.json C4L-4; runC-plan.json session_lead_decisions[35] (sent to this triage).
items.root_cause_at_head: packages/memory/src/retrieval.ts:180 and :214 keep a lesson only when r.project_id equals the request's projectId (no joined projects); chat recall reads lessons through withJoined (packages/runtime/src/conversation/scope.ts) but the session's memory request passes the kept project's id alone.
items.fix_sketch: Retrieval takes a set of project ids: the request's project plus the projects joined into it (the same withJoined scope chat uses, read from projects.joined_into or joined_from); the session's brief builder passes that set; lessons stay canonical on their own project (ADR 0117's amendment kept: nothing is moved or copied). A lesson of a closed project is ranked like the kept project's own. Undo of the join drops it again (the scope is read at each call).
items.test_boundary: Composed runtime test: two projects with a lesson each, Make one project (the project.join command), then the kept project's next specialist request (the stand-in provider's captured brief or the memory block of the request) carries the closed project's lesson; after Undo of the join it does not; a memory unit case for the project-id set.
items.notes: d1109-onerepo-join's subsystem (the github group's journey); sent to this triage by session lead decision 35, kept here beside recall's withJoined; the session lead may move it to the github group's join area. Cut line: may end not_done with the failing test.

How it ended: Done.' for a session in which 'Write the welcome page' also failed; chat then says 'I need to correct my earlier answers ... The CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES sentence for the C14d half ('Your earlier replies rest on lookups not shown again here: before you call one wrong or unconfirmed, look it up in this turn; when a hit leaves something out, open it.') is built with L4-chat-203's change to the same constant (l4-chat-depth owns depth.ts).

decisions: A yes after a reply of chat's own that asks something (its text, without a read-back, ends with a question; no card, notice, action or app offer) goes to the model with the history, never 'Yes to what?'; the forwarded turn inherits the previous turn's recordsRead, so every change it leads to is read back first. 'Yes to what?' stays for a yes after a statement, a notice, an answered card or nothing, with a next step in its words. Design §3.9's '"yes" with no card' line and user-guide.md:400 change accordingly (the session lead edits the design document from this area's notes).

The claim guard gains two kinds: 'asks' (a yes asked for in words to make a change) and 'absent' (a 'not there / can't find / Should I look?' reply in a turn that offered recall and called neither recall tool); one nudge each, inside the turn's model calls and its budget; a claim still standing gives the true line as today. Clarifying questions stay free.

Prompt (conversation-agent.md, this area's sections, and CHAT_RECALL_RULES): look it up in this turn instead of offering to; never ask for a yes in words; only the app writes 'The app did:'; never describe tool calls, their order or refusals; never name a tool; all asserted verbatim on the request.

Recall's lines are worded as the screens word them: a session line names its failed tasks; a questions card's line carries its question; the From line names the records the reply rests on among the turn's hits, opened or strong and named by title (ADR 0114 'Sources', dated amendment).

decisions: A yes is judged against what the person was shown: the stored 'at most' is the CHF on the line (rounded up to the centime); a Go ahead re-asks only when the model changed or the shown figure would change; the pass's budget is the yes's 'at most', capped by the room.

The fast model never asks in words: the thinking_longer fact and answer_thoroughly's definition say who acts. An ask-only backstop in code (a dated amendment to ADR 0114's 'Who decides', for the session lead's review): a typed quick answer that ended without answer_thoroughly on a line whose words show a failure, plan, comparison or review need gets the app's own ask line with Go ahead when the rung asks first, or Think it through when it would go ahead; a pattern never spends, nothing runs before the person's yes (the owner's answer 2: 'warn/ask first').

The thorough pass is told what it is: its own facts line ('this_answer: the closer look on Sonnet the person said yes to ...') in place of the quick pass's thinking_longer line, and CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES saying it is the closer look; the fast request stays byte-identical.
Answer now never earns a next-rung offer; only a pass whose budget line wrapped it up does.
The history window moves in steps of 6 turns, a pure function of the stored rows (the same after a restart), so quick turns read the history from the prompt cache.
